G.name: Mass per metre
G.explain: How much one metre of section weighs. Sets the self-weight in your structure and much of the cost; steel is bought by the kilo.

h.name: Depth
h.explain: The overall depth of the section. Sets the structural depth of a floor or roof and so the storey height. Deeper section: stiffer against deflection.

b.name: Width
b.explain: The flange width. Adds to the stiffness about the weak axis and sets how much room you have for bearings and connections.

tw.name: Web thickness
tw.explain: The thickness of the vertical web. The web mainly carries shear; a thicker web resists more at supports and under point loads.

tf.name: Flange thickness
tf.explain: The thickness of the horizontal flanges. The flanges carry most of the bending moment; mind the flange thickness for bolt holes and welds.

t.name: Wall thickness
t.explain: The wall thickness of a hollow section or tube. At the same outer size a thicker wall gives more strength and stiffness, and more weight.

D.name: Outside diameter
D.explain: The outer size of a round tube. A tube is equally stiff in every direction; useful for columns and trusses.

A.name: Area
A.explain: The cross-sectional area. Sets how much axial force (tension or compression) the section can carry and, with the density, its weight.

Iy.name: Second moment of area, strong axis
Iy.explain: How stiff the section is against bending about the strong axis. Use it to estimate beam deflection: twice as large means half the deflection.

Iz.name: Second moment of area, weak axis
Iz.explain: The stiffness about the weak axis. Important for columns, which usually buckle about this axis.

Wy.name: Section modulus, strong axis
Wy.explain: Links bending moment to stress: stress = moment / W. Use it to check whether a beam is strong enough.

Wz.name: Section modulus, weak axis
Wz.explain: Like W about the strong axis, but for bending about the weak axis, for example wind on the flange.

iy.name: Radius of gyration, strong axis
iy.explain: √(I/A): how far, on average, the material lies from the axis. Needed for slenderness and so for buckling about the strong axis.

iz.name: Radius of gyration, weak axis
iz.explain: √(I/A) about the weak axis. Usually governs column buckling: smaller i, earlier buckling.

timber.title: Timber
timber.flagged: No value in the Vademecum table fits this size. The size may not belong in the table. A, W and I are still calculated exactly for a b × h rectangle.
timber.method: Sizes (b × h) from the table; A, W and I calculated exactly for a rectangle. Every table cell was checked against this calculation.

explain.A: The area of the cross-section, b × h. Sets how much tension or compression the member can carry and, with the density of the timber, the weight per metre.
explain.Wy: Section modulus about the strong axis, b·h²/6. Links bending moment to stress: stress = moment / W. Use it to check whether a beam on edge is strong enough.
explain.Iy: Second moment of area about the strong axis, b·h³/12. Says how stiff the beam is against deflection. Because h counts to the third power, a deeper beam helps far more than a wider one.
explain.Wz: Section modulus about the weak axis, h·b²/6. Matters when the member lies flat or is loaded sideways.
explain.Iz: Second moment of area about the weak axis, h·b³/12. Usually governs buckling of a stud or column, and lateral torsional buckling of slender beams.

timber.hatch: Timber hatch from the Vademecum (NEN 2302). The source gives no separate hatch for glulam.

sheets.title: Profiled steel sheets
sheets.Iy: Second moment of area per metre
sheets.flagged: The Vademecum column header gives contradictory units. Iy and Wy are read here as ×10⁴ mm⁴/m and ×10³ mm³/m, and the source does not say which stress σ is. Do not use these values without checking the source.
sheets.units: Iy and Wy per metre of sheet width, according to our reading of the column header. Not yet confirmed.

explain.h: The height of the profile, from the bottom to the top of the rib. A deeper sheet is stiffer and can span further.
explain.t: The thickness of the steel the sheet is formed from. A thicker sheet is stronger and stiffer, but also heavier.
explain.Iy: Second moment of area per metre of sheet width. Says how stiff the sheet is against deflection between supports.
explain.Wy: Section modulus per metre of sheet width. Links bending moment to stress: stress = moment / W.
explain.sigma: The source does not say which stress this is. Do not use this value until its meaning is clear.

sheets.unitNote: Unit read here as {unit}. The Vademecum column header is contradictory.
sheets.sigmaNote: Meaning and unit not explained in the source.
